strategicLeadership.text: How strong is executive leadership support for AI initiatives?

options.label: No awareness or interest from leadership
Minimal interest - low priority
Moderate support - acknowledged importance
Strong support - actively championed
Full commitment - strategic imperative with resources

strategicLeadership.text: Do you have a documented AI strategy aligned with business objectives?

options.label: No AI strategy exists
Informal discussions about AI
Strategy being developed with basic objectives
Documented strategy with clear business alignment
Comprehensive strategy fully integrated with business goals

strategicLeadership.text: How does your leadership team understand and communicate AI's transformative potential?

options.label: No understanding or communication of AI capabilities
Aware of AI hype but limited knowledge or communication
Basic understanding with occasional AI vision messaging
Good grasp of AI impact with consistent communication
Deep expertise with inspiring AI narrative embedded in culture

useCasePortfolio.text: How well have you identified and prioritized AI use cases?

options.label: No use cases identified
Generic use cases with no prioritization
Some use cases identified and prioritized
Well-defined use cases with business cases
Portfolio of use cases with clear ROI and strategic priorities

useCasePortfolio.text: What is your approach to balancing quick wins versus transformational AI initiatives?

options.label: No structured approach to portfolio balance
Focus only on easy wins or only on long-term
Mix of quick wins and longer-term projects
Strategic portfolio balancing short and long-term value
Optimized portfolio with innovation pipeline and clear roadmap

useCasePortfolio.text: How effective is your approach to scaling successful AI pilots to production?

options.label: No pilots scaled to production
Ad-hoc scaling attempts with limited success
Some pilots successfully scaled with lessons learned
Structured scaling methodology with clear criteria
Industrialized deployment pipeline with proven track record

dataFoundation.text: How would you rate the overall quality and governance of your organizational data?

options.label: Poor quality with no governance
Below average quality with basic policies being developed
Moderate quality with governance framework in place
Good quality with mature governance and active enforcement
Excellent quality with advanced governance and automation

dataFoundation.text: How accessible and democratized is data across your organization?

options.label: Highly siloed - data trapped in departments
Mostly siloed with limited sharing mechanisms
Partially integrated with some cross-functional access
Well integrated with good data accessibility
Fully democratized with comprehensive self-service access

dataFoundation.text: How mature are your data pipelines, architecture, and quality monitoring?

options.label: No automated pipelines or quality monitoring
Manual processes with basic databases
Basic automated pipelines with data warehouse
Well-orchestrated pipelines with data lake and monitoring
Advanced architecture with real-time streaming and AI-based monitoring

techInfrastructure.text: How mature is your cloud infrastructure and computational resources for AI/ML workloads?

options.label: No cloud infrastructure or dedicated AI compute resources
Basic cloud adoption with CPU resources only
Hybrid cloud with some GPU/TPU access available
Cloud-first with dedicated GPU/TPU infrastructure
Cloud-native with advanced distributed computing and AI accelerators

techInfrastructure.text: How scalable and modern is your technology infrastructure?

options.label: Not scalable with monolithic legacy applications
Manual scaling with mostly legacy architecture
Some auto-scaling with mix of legacy and modern
Good auto-scaling with microservices architecture
Fully elastic cloud-native with containerization and orchestration

techInfrastructure.text: How advanced are your DevOps/MLOps capabilities and ML platforms?

options.label: No DevOps practices or ML platforms
Basic CI/CD pipelines with individual ML tools used ad-hoc
Established DevOps with some ML tools and frameworks adopted
Advanced DevOps with integrated ML platform for development
Full MLOps/AIOps with enterprise ML platform for end-to-end lifecycle

governanceRisk.text: How prepared are you for AI-related regulatory compliance and risk management?

options.label: Unaware of regulations with no risk assessment
Aware of regulations but no compliance or risk framework
Understanding regulations with basic risk assessment framework
Compliance program in development with systematic risk management
Full compliance with proactive risk management and continuous monitoring

governanceRisk.text: What security measures and data privacy frameworks are in place for AI systems?

options.label: No specific security or privacy framework for AI
Standard IT security with basic privacy awareness
Some AI-specific security with privacy policies in development
Comprehensive AI security with strong privacy controls
Advanced security and privacy-preserving AI techniques with continuous monitoring

governanceRisk.text: How mature is your AI model governance and audit capability?

options.label: No model governance or audit trails
Basic logging of AI outputs
Monitoring of key AI systems with some documentation
Comprehensive monitoring with audit trails and model registry
Advanced governance with automated compliance checking and full auditability

responsibleAI.text: How mature is your AI ethics framework and governance?

options.label: No consideration of AI ethics
Aware of ethical issues but no framework
Basic ethical guidelines being developed
Formal ethics framework with governance oversight
Comprehensive ethics governance with active board and enforcement

responsibleAI.text: How do you address bias, fairness, and transparency in AI systems?

options.label: No consideration of bias, fairness, or transparency
Aware of issues but no processes or testing
Basic bias testing and some explainability efforts
Systematic bias detection with transparency mechanisms
Continuous fairness monitoring with advanced explainability and stakeholder engagement

responsibleAI.text: What is your approach to stakeholder impact assessment and responsible AI practices?

options.label: No stakeholder impact assessment or responsible AI practices
Minimal consideration of stakeholder impacts
Basic impact assessment for major initiatives
Systematic stakeholder impact analysis with accountability structures
Comprehensive responsible AI framework with continuous stakeholder engagement

peopleSkills.text: What is the current level of AI skills and expertise in your organization?

options.label: No AI skills or expertise
Limited skills - few individuals with basic knowledge
Developing capabilities - small team building skills
Solid expertise - dedicated AI/ML team with proven track record
Advanced capabilities - centers of excellence with deep expertise

peopleSkills.text: How strong is your investment in AI training, upskilling, and data literacy?

options.label: No training budget or data literacy programs
Minimal ad-hoc training with low data literacy
Regular training programs with growing data literacy
Comprehensive learning paths with widespread data-driven culture
Continuous learning ecosystem with certifications and data-first culture

changeManagement.text: How would you describe your organizational learning culture and adaptability?

options.label: Resistant to change - traditional approaches strongly preferred
Slow to adopt - very cautious about new approaches
Moderately adaptive - open to learning with support
Learning-oriented - continuous improvement mindset embedded
Innovation-driven - experimentation actively encouraged and rewarded

changeManagement.text: How effective is your change management capability for AI transformation?

options.label: No change management processes or support
Ad-hoc approach to change with limited success
Basic change management framework being applied
Structured change management with proven success
Agile change management - highly effective with AI-specific expertise

changeManagement.text: How well do teams collaborate cross-functionally on AI initiatives?

options.label: No cross-functional collaboration - strong silos
Minimal collaboration - mostly department-isolated work
Some cross-functional projects with mixed success
Strong collaborative culture with effective cross-functional teams
Seamless integration with high-performing cross-functional AI teams

valueRealization.text: How do you measure success and track ROI for AI initiatives?

options.label: No success metrics or ROI tracking defined
Technical metrics only with no business value tracking
Mix of technical and business metrics with basic ROI
Clear business KPIs with comprehensive ROI tracking
Sophisticated value framework with real-time ROI dashboards and optimization

valueRealization.text: What is your approach to AI business case development and value modeling?

options.label: No business cases required or value modeling
High-level cost estimates only
Basic ROI calculations and simple business cases
Comprehensive business cases with NPV analysis and benefits tracking
Sophisticated value modeling with scenario analysis and continuous optimization
